sites.ownership: One GitRunState is retained by its owned operation/grace sources and asynchronous communication/wait callbacks; it contains no UI or workspace reference.
sites.justification: Communication completion is distinct from successful child wait. User-cancelled mutations retain the original deadline; only terminal completion removes owned sources and takes the optional callback. The callback runs after the RefCell borrow ends. Held checkpoints exist only in tests.

sites.ownership: RIT-GEN-007 test fixtures own only synthetic temporary files, child handles, event observations and held test continuations; compiled only in the test module.
sites.justification: The controlled-child handshake and bounded GLib pumping exercise the shared production runner. Teardown force-exits and waits for the fixture child; result and event slots record terminal ordering without holding application windows. Filesystem probes are confined to the fixture directory, never user documents or portal paths.

sites.ownership: The typed /app/bin/git runner owns this subprocess and its stdin/stdout/stderr capture until communication settles and uncancelled wait succeeds.
sites.justification: Only typed production operations construct argv with fixed environment and sandbox Git. Cancellation and deadlines retain child supervision; mutation timeout waits through TERM and force-exit grace. Output caps are checked after communicate buffering; bounded streaming remains separate P3 work.

sites.ownership: The cfg(test) boundary wrapper owns a reference to an observed test child for fixture teardown.
sites.justification: Only the approved subprocess boundary exposes force-and-wait cleanup; GTK fixtures cannot access Gio subprocess control directly. Test teardown reaps observed children even after an assertion failure, while normal completion remains owned by the actual supervisor.
